correctness.rationale: Arnold's Theorem 3.1 gives the necessary lower threshold and contractivity when \(K=1\). For finite \(Q\), setting \(\beta=p/Q\) in the same weighted-shift family gives exact constant \(K_Q=Q/(Q-p)\le K\) and endpoint failure via the harmonic orbit sum. The square-zero block has exact \(p\)-constant \(K\) and every finite exponent. On the \(\ell^p\)-sum, \(p\)-orbit sums add exactly, so the optimal constant is \(K\); finite \(q\)-bounds transfer by \((a^p+b^p)^{q/p}\le2^{q/p-1}(a^q+b^q)\), while the invariant shift summand preserves failure at \(Q\). Thus the full interval and \(\infty\) are realized.
correctness.risk: The classification concerns the supremum \(q_*\), not whether a general operator attains its endpoint.

final_claim: For fixed \(1\le p<\infty\), the feasible pairs of optimal \(p\)-absolute-Cesaro constant and supremal self-improvement exponent are exactly: \(K=1\) forces \(q_*=\infty\), while for every \(K>1\), every \(Q\in[pK/(K-1),\infty]\) and only those \(Q\) occur, already for positive operators on \(\ell^p\).
limitations: Endpoint membership is not classified in general; finite constructed endpoints deliberately fail strongly.
No irreducibility or invertibility restriction is claimed.
